what_it_does: Reads a Chandrayaan-2 PDS4 product: first the XML label (image size, pixel type, resolution, corner coordinates, sun angles, capture time), then the pixels using the size/type/offset the label states. Built on pds4_tools, with a targeted lxml lookup for ISRO-specific fields pds4_tools misses.
why_it_matters: Most competing teams claim to parse PDS labels but really just load pixels with a generic image reader. Every later step depends on the real label fields.
done_when: tests/test_pds_real.py passes on real OHRC, TMC-2 and IIRS labels with >=6 fields marked as read from the label; a truncated label raises PdsParseError; a 1 KB window reads from a multi-GB file in <100 ms.

what_it_does: Reads older PDS3 products (.img + .lbl text label) used by SELENE/Kaguya: image size, bits per pixel, pixel type and where the pixels start in the file (the ^IMAGE pointer). Labels via pvl; pixels via our own memory-mapped window reader (planetaryimage is not used: it loads the whole image and cannot read windows).
why_it_matters: SELENE is one of the two reference sources the problem statement names, and it only ships as PDS3.
done_when: A real SELENE TC label parses and its ^IMAGE offset lands on the pixel data, proven by reproducing the MINIMUM/MAXIMUM/AVERAGE/STDEV statistics JAXA wrote in the label; every ^IMAGE pointer form, byte order and band interleave is covered by synthetic tests.

what_it_does: Handles OHRC images: Chandrayaan-2's sharpest camera. 0.25 m per pixel, black-and-white (500-800 nm), very long narrow strips (e.g. 79,796 x 12,000 px).
why_it_matters: One of the three source cameras the problem statement names. OHRC <-> LRO NAC is our Easy benchmark tier and credibility check.
done_when: A real OHRC product (e.g. ch2_ohr_ncp_20211228T2209123959_d_img_d18) parses and a window of it reads correctly.

what_it_does: Handles TMC-2 (Terrain Mapping Camera) images: ~5 m per pixel (4.43 m/px on real labels), 20 km wide, black-and-white, photographs each area from 3 angles. Products reach 191,483 x 4,000 px.
why_it_matters: TMC-2 is where we aim to be first: no published work registers it against SELENE, and the best attempt against LRO NAC reached only a 2.8% inlier ratio.
done_when: A real TMC-2 label (191,483 x 4,000, 4.43 m/px) parses and a windowed read succeeds.

what_it_does: Handles IIRS infrared spectrometer cubes: ~80 m per pixel, ~250-256 colour bands from 0.8 to 5.0 micrometres, stored band-by-band or interleaved (BSQ/BIL/BIP). Read with the spectral library via the ENVI .hdr file.
why_it_matters: The third source camera the problem statement names. It looks nothing like a normal camera image, which makes it the hardest to match.
done_when: A real IIRS .hdr/.xml parses; the band count comes from the label; both a single band and the full cube can be read.

what_it_does: Loads NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Narrow Angle Camera images (0.5 m per pixel) as the fixed reference image, into the same SceneMeta structure as the Chandrayaan-2 source image.
why_it_matters: The reference named in the problem statement. Loading source and reference into one common structure means the rest of the pipeline does not care which camera is which.
done_when: The real NAC product M1404744695RC.IMG loads into a SceneMeta with the same shape as a Chandrayaan-2 source.

what_it_does: Loads LRO Wide Angle Camera images (~100 m per pixel, several colour bands) as a reference.
why_it_matters: A reference at IIRS's resolution: IIRS <-> WAC is our Medium benchmark tier.
done_when: A WAC product loads into SceneMeta and an IIRS <-> WAC pair can be built.

what_it_does: Loads SELENE/Kaguya Terrain Camera images (~7.4-10 m per pixel, PDS3) as a reference, and gathers real TMC-2 and SELENE TC images that cover the same ground.
why_it_matters: TMC-2 <-> SELENE TC (~2:1 scale) is the pairing nobody has published. It is our headline contribution.
done_when: A real SELENE TC .img + .lbl loads into SceneMeta; at least 3 genuinely overlapping TMC-2 <-> SELENE TC pairs are downloaded with their overlap recorded.

what_it_does: Loads SELENE Multiband Imager images (~20-62 m per pixel, several colour bands) as a reference.
why_it_matters: Stretch goal: MI has never been tried against any Chandrayaan-2 camera.
done_when: An MI product loads into SceneMeta with its band information.

what_it_does: Works out which of the 7 cameras a file came from using its product ID (ch2_ohr_*, ch2_tmc_*, ch2_iir_*, M*RC.IMG for NAC, ...) and looks up that camera's resolution, bands and swath in configs/instruments.yaml. Also gives the resolution ratio between any two cameras (gsd_ratio).
why_it_matters: Lets one pipeline handle every camera from config, with no camera-specific code branches; the problem statement asks for a generic solution. The ratio feeds matcher routing and the cascade.
done_when: All 7 cameras resolve from real product IDs; gsd_ratio('OHRC','IIRS') is ~320.

what_it_does: Cuts huge images into overlapping tiles (default 1024 px with 128 px overlap), skips mostly-empty tiles, and remembers where each tile sits so match points can be mapped back to full-image coordinates.
why_it_matters: Real products are far too big for any matcher in one go (TMC-2 191k x 4k, OHRC 80k x 12k, NAC 104k x 5k px).
done_when: Tiles of a 191k x 4k product are generated lazily with bounded memory; tile_to_global maps points back exactly.

what_it_does: Given a Chandrayaan-2 image's ground outline, asks NASA's PDS Orbital Data Explorer (ODE) web API which reference images cover the same ground. Free, no login.
why_it_matters: Finding overlapping image pairs by hand is slow and error-prone.
done_when: Returns at least one real NAC product ID for a known lunar bounding box.

what_it_does: Downloads and crops lunar elevation maps to a scene's ground area: LOLA (118 m/px, whole Moon), SLDEM2015 (59 m/px, within +/-60 deg latitude) and Kaguya ARD from the public s3://astrogeo-ard bucket (no AWS account needed).
why_it_matters: Elevation is needed for slope/aspect (physics-based filtering) and to cross-check label metadata.
done_when: Returns an elevation array lined up with a given scene's ground area, with the DEM source recorded.

what_it_does: Reads each image's sun position (sun azimuth, incidence angle) from its label, and computes how different the lighting is between source and reference (illumination_delta: change in incidence, azimuth and phase).
why_it_matters: Changing sun angle is the problem statement's #1 challenge. The lighting difference decides which matcher gets used.
done_when: On a real label, incidence and azimuth are read (not defaulted) and GeometryLayers.source == 'label'.

what_it_does: Produces per-pixel angles: incidence (sun to ground), emission (ground to camera) and phase (sun-ground-camera). Taken from the label where present, otherwise computed from SPICE spacecraft data (spiceypy) or interpolated from the image corners as a labelled approximation. Records which method was used.
why_it_matters: The physics-based filter and shadow assistance need angles per pixel, not one number per image.
done_when: GeometryLayers holds the angle arrays with source set to 'label', 'spice' or 'derived'; works with ISIS3 not installed.

what_it_does: Computes, for every elevation-map pixel, how steep the ground is (slope) and which direction it faces (aspect), using gdaldem or richdem.
why_it_matters: Direct input to the physics-based outlier filter, our main new idea.
done_when: Slope of a synthetic constant-gradient DEM equals the analytic value within 0.1 deg.

what_it_does: Draws each image's ground outline from its corner lat/lon and measures how much the two overlap. Pairs below a minimum overlap are rejected before any matching runs.
why_it_matters: Matching images that do not show the same ground wastes time and produces fake matches (failure mode #10).
done_when: A non-overlapping pair is rejected with a clear reason and zero matcher calls.

what_it_does: Handles Moon coordinate systems (selenographic CRS via pyproj) and performs an explicit reprojection step. Raw Chandrayaan-2 products carry only corner lat/lon with no map projection applied, so none is ever assumed.
why_it_matters: A wrong or missing projection puts the output in the wrong place (failure mode #9). Needed for a correct GeoTIFF and GeoJSON.
done_when: Reprojecting a scene and back returns corner coordinates within 1e-6 deg.

what_it_does: Before matching, compares the two cameras' resolution ratio with the range each matcher is known to handle, and flags pairs that must go through the cascade (e.g. OHRC <-> IIRS at ~320:1).
why_it_matters: No matcher has been shown to work across a 100x+ scale gap; direct attempts gave 0 inliers (failure mode #3).
done_when: An OHRC <-> IIRS request is flagged as extreme-scale before any matcher runs.

what_it_does: Works out the true alignment two independent ways, from label geometry (using both OHRC corner-quality levels) and from a DEM re-projection, and reports how far apart they are as an uncertainty bound. This is our ground truth.
why_it_matters: Labels can be wrong or out of date (failure mode #8). No public ground truth exists, so this is how we build ours without trusting a single source.
done_when: Label-derived and DEM-derived transforms are reported together with their disagreement; a deliberately injected label error is caught.

what_it_does: Boosts contrast region by region (contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalisation), stretches brightness, and scales pixels to 0-1 floats.
why_it_matters: Evens out lighting so both dark and bright areas show detail. First line of defence against sun-angle changes.
done_when: CLAHE measurably raises local contrast in a shadowed crop; output is float32 in 0-1, as ImagePlane requires.

what_it_does: Converts an image into a map of edges and structure based on phase rather than brightness (via phasepack), plus a maximum-index map used by RIFT2.
why_it_matters: Survives brightness and contrast differences between sensors and sun angles, and still works on low-contrast terrain. It is the input to the RIFT2 matcher.
done_when: Phase-congruency maps of an image and a strongly gamma-shifted copy correlate >0.9, where raw pixel correlation is much lower.

what_it_does: Describes each pixel by how similar it is to its neighbours instead of by its brightness.
why_it_matters: Lets images from very different sensors (black-and-white camera vs infrared spectrometer) be compared directly.
done_when: A synthetic cross-sensor pair matches better on the MIND version than on raw pixels.

what_it_does: Finds shadowed areas (near-zero brightness, little local variation, optionally checked against the sun angle) and marks them so matching skips them or treats them as low-confidence.
why_it_matters: Shadows move with the sun, so matches inside them are usually wrong (failure mode #2).
done_when: On a crater-interior crop the mask overlaps a hand-drawn mask with IoU > 0.7.

what_it_does: Estimates signal-to-noise for each IIRS band and drops the noisy ones.
why_it_matters: Many IIRS bands are too noisy to find features in (failure mode #4).
done_when: Per-band SNR is computed on a real IIRS cube and the chosen band list is logged.

what_it_does: Blends the good IIRS bands into one black-and-white image that resembles what a normal camera would see.
why_it_matters: No single IIRS band looks like a camera image; two separate teams got 0 inliers matching raw cubes (failure mode #5).
done_when: The composite yields more keypoints than the best single band on a real IIRS cube; the band list is recorded in preprocess_chain.

what_it_does: Scores how much texture a tile has (gradient energy / entropy). A low score switches matching to the phase-congruency path.
why_it_matters: Smooth mare plains have few features, so ordinary detectors find too few points (failure mode #1).
done_when: A flat mare crop scores low texture and triggers the fallback path.

what_it_does: Scores how self-similar a tile is (autocorrelation), e.g. a field of similar-looking craters. A high score makes matching stricter.
why_it_matters: In repeating terrain one crater looks like another, which causes false matches (failure mode #11).
done_when: A crater-field crop scores high repetitiveness.

what_it_does: Classic SIFT feature matching plus RANSAC (OpenCV / vismatch). The floor every other method is measured against.
why_it_matters: Every real lunar registration paper uses it as the baseline; our ablation study starts here.
done_when: Recovers a known synthetic homography to <1 px RMSE on the P0-T05 fixture.

what_it_does: Extra classical detectors, selectable in config, for comparison.
why_it_matters: AKAZE is competitive with SIFT near the equator; ORB is included for completeness only.
done_when: All three run and are selectable via config.

what_it_does: Learned (AI) matcher and the shipped default, run through vismatch. Apache-2.0 including its weights; runs on CPU or GPU.
why_it_matters: Fastest learned matcher, and licence-safe for ISRO to reuse.
done_when: Runs on CPU and GPU, returns a valid MatchSet, and beats SIFT on a synthetic lighting-shifted pair.

what_it_does: Dense transformer matcher (LoFTR / EfficientLoFTR) that needs no keypoint detector. Never used on its own for extreme low-sun images.
why_it_matters: Strong on low-texture ground, but documented to fail almost completely at very low sun elevation (failure mode #17).
done_when: Runs, and the regime selector only routes it to non-extreme lighting.

what_it_does: Small, fast matcher for machines with no GPU.
why_it_matters: Safety net in case the demo laptop has no GPU.
done_when: The full pipeline completes on CPU within the demo time budget.

what_it_does: Matcher built for images from different sensor types, working on phase-congruency maps. Uses a vendored copy of RIFT2-python pinned to a commit SHA.
why_it_matters: Handles non-linear brightness differences (camera vs spectrometer). A 2025 benchmark found classical RIFT beating the best deep method at high resolution.
done_when: Beats SIFT by inlier ratio on a synthetic cross-sensor pair; the vendored SHA is recorded.

what_it_does: Statistical score of how well two images line up that works across sensor types. Used to check alignment quality after registration, NOT to find matches.
why_it_matters: Gives a quality score for cross-sensor pairs where no ground truth exists.
done_when: MI on an aligned cross-sensor pair is higher than on a deliberately misaligned one; exposed as an after-the-fact quality metric.

what_it_does: Detects craters and checks that the craters around each match form the same pattern in both images.
why_it_matters: Craters are stable, lighting-robust landmarks unique to the Moon; this catches false matches RANSAC lets through in repetitive terrain.
done_when: Crater-neighbourhood checks reject matches RANSAC alone accepts on a repetitive-terrain subset; does nothing when too few craters are found.

what_it_does: Picks the matcher automatically from the sun-angle difference, scale ratio and sensor types: normal lighting -> LightGlue; low sun / polar -> LightGlue or LoFTR on phase-congruency images; different sensors -> RIFT2; scale gap >= 4x -> cascade. Rules live in configs/regimes.yaml.
why_it_matters: No single matcher wins everywhere; the evidence shows each is best in a different situation. Routing instead of hardcoding also keeps the pipeline generic.
done_when: A polar-lighting pair routes to the polar path; an OHRC <-> IIRS request routes to the cascade, never to a direct match.

what_it_does: Crosses huge resolution gaps in steps instead of one jump: OHRC -> TMC-2 (~20:1) -> SELENE TC (~2:1) or IIRS (~16:1) -> LRO NAC/WAC. Chains the transforms together and adds up the uncertainty from each step.
why_it_matters: Direct OHRC <-> IIRS (~320:1) gave 0 inliers for two separate teams. Each step stays within what matchers can handle.
done_when: A direct OHRC <-> IIRS request is intercepted and routed via TMC-2; the chained transform on synthetic data matches the analytic result; per-step and total error are both reported.

what_it_does: Aligns OHRC to LRO NAC first to pin down true Moon coordinates, then ties TMC-2 and IIRS into that frame through their known relationship to OHRC (same spacecraft, same orbit, near-same time).
why_it_matters: OHRC <-> NAC is the only pairing with strong repeated evidence, so it serves as the anchor. This is a design hypothesis to test, not a proven method.
done_when: Bridge mode runs and its result is reported separately from direct registration.

what_it_does: Checks whether matched features agree on orientation before RANSAC. If the rotation is extreme, simulates rotated/tilted views (ASIFT style) or switches to a rotation-invariant descriptor.
why_it_matters: Different orbit tracks and pushbroom cameras produce large rotations between images (failure mode #6; the problem statement's viewpoint challenge).
done_when: A 60-deg-rotated synthetic pair that plain SIFT fails on is recovered.

what_it_does: When matches collapse because the images are further apart than expected, widens the search using a rough position from DEM/SPICE before fine matching.
why_it_matters: Label position errors can put images hundreds of pixels apart (failure mode #7).
done_when: A pair with an injected 500 px position error still registers.

what_it_does: Keeps a match only if its best candidate is clearly better than the second-best (Lowe ratio test), and only if both points pick each other as best (mutual nearest neighbour).
why_it_matters: The cheapest robust filter; removes most obviously ambiguous matches.
done_when: Both filters reduce the outlier fraction on a fixture.

what_it_does: Automatically tightens the ratio-test threshold in tiles with a high repetitiveness score.
why_it_matters: Repeating craters produce false matches that pass a normal threshold (failure mode #11).
done_when: A crater-field crop scores high repetitiveness and receives a tightened threshold.

what_it_does: Fits the transform between the images while ignoring wrong matches: repeatedly tries small random subsets and keeps the model most matches agree with. MAGSAC++ (OpenCV USAC) removes the need to hand-tune the error threshold.
why_it_matters: Even after filtering, many matches are wrong, and one bad match can wreck a plain fit.
done_when: Recovers a known synthetic homography to <1 px RMSE; MAGSAC beats plain RANSAC with 70% outliers.

what_it_does: Three shapes of transform: affine (shift, rotate, scale, shear), homography (adds perspective) and TPS thin-plate spline (smooth local bending). Chooses between them from how the leftover errors are spread.
why_it_matters: Crater relief bends the image locally in ways a single global transform cannot fix.
done_when: TPS reduces leftover error compared with a homography on a synthetic relief-distorted pair.

what_it_does: For every match, looks up terrain slope/aspect and sun/view angles at both ends. Throws out physically impossible matches (e.g. a steep sunlit slope matched to a flat shadowed plain) and down-weights doubtful ones before MAGSAC. Where sun angle and a DEM both exist, also uses predicted shadow shapes to help matching. Switches itself off, with a note, when no DEM is available.
why_it_matters: Our main new idea: RANSAC only checks that matches agree geometrically, not that they make physical sense. No published general pipeline does this for cross-sensor lunar images.
owner: Member B (Member A joins from Phase 3)
done_when: On a repetitive crater-field subset, false-positive inliers drop measurably compared with RANSAC alone, reported as inlier precision (Ablation Experiment 3).

what_it_does: Splits the image into an N x N grid and keeps only the top-k most confident matches in each cell.
why_it_matters: The problem statement requires match points spread evenly; this stops one dense cluster from dominating the fit.
done_when: Coverage of a deliberately clustered synthetic match set rises from <0.15 to >0.6; no cell ever holds more than k matches.

what_it_does: For grid cells left with zero matches, searches just that area again with a looser threshold.
why_it_matters: Avoids the failure case the problem statement illustrates: a dense cluster plus empty regions.
done_when: Coverage improves after the refill pass on a fixture with deliberately empty regions.

what_it_does: Connects the final points into triangles and flags very large triangles as under-covered areas.
why_it_matters: A second, independent coverage check alongside grid occupancy.
done_when: max_delaunay_gap_px is filled in and falls as spatial coverage rises on fixtures.

what_it_does: Alternative way to pick points: repeatedly chooses the point furthest from those already chosen.
why_it_matters: Gives a comparison against the grid method.
done_when: Selectable via config and compared against grid retention in the report.

what_it_does: Around each matched pixel, computes normalised cross-correlation on a small grid and fits a parabola to find the true peak between pixels.
why_it_matters: The problem statement demands sub-pixel accuracy.
done_when: Recovers a known sub-pixel shift to <0.1 px on the fixture.

what_it_does: Estimates the remaining shift (and scale, via log-polar) in the frequency domain using upsampled phase correlation (skimage).
why_it_matters: A second, independent sub-pixel method that also catches small scale errors.
done_when: The leftover shift after correction is smaller than before, measured on the fixture.

what_it_does: OpenCV cornerSubPix: iteratively nudges each corner point to its exact sub-pixel position.
why_it_matters: A third independent method for the comparison table.
done_when: Runs and appears in the sub-pixel method comparison table.

what_it_does: OpenCV findTransformECC: refines the alignment while compensating for brightness and contrast differences. Needs a rough alignment first, so it is used only for refinement.
why_it_matters: Built for exactly the lighting-variation challenge in the problem statement.
done_when: Reduces leftover error on a lighting-shifted pair that already has a rough alignment; fails gracefully when the starting alignment is poor.

what_it_does: Refines the whole transform (the 8 homography parameters) with scipy least_squares, instead of individual points.
why_it_matters: A fourth method that works at a different level: the global transform rather than point positions.
done_when: Global RMSE decreases after refinement on real data.

what_it_does: Shifts a real Chandrayaan-2 image by a known fraction of a pixel, e.g. (0.37, -0.62), and measures how accurately the pipeline recovers that shift.
why_it_matters: No public sub-pixel ground truth exists, so this is the honest way to prove the problem statement's sub-pixel requirement.
done_when: At least two of the four methods recover (0.37, -0.62) to <0.1 px; Metrics.subpixel_recovery_err_px is filled from a real measurement on real imagery.

what_it_does: Matches a plain grey image against the reference. It must find almost no inliers.
why_it_matters: If this 'succeeds', the pipeline is broken. A competitor's shared-mask bug produced fake 100% inlier rates (failure mode #19).
done_when: Runs on every benchmark execution and is recorded in RegistrationResult.gates.

what_it_does: Matches pure random noise against the reference. It must find almost no inliers.
why_it_matters: Same purpose as the blank-image test, with a textured input that fools naive matchers.
done_when: Runs on every benchmark execution and is recorded in RegistrationResult.gates.

what_it_does: Shifts the image by a known 5 px; the recovered transform must move by about 5 px, not 0 and not 50.
why_it_matters: Catches a pipeline that ignores its input or is unstable.
done_when: The result is recorded, and a deliberately broken pipeline fails it.

what_it_does: Matches an image against itself: RMSE must be ~0 and inlier ratio ~1.
why_it_matters: Anything else means a basic bug.
done_when: Runs on every benchmark execution and is recorded in RegistrationResult.gates.

what_it_does: After fitting, compares the estimated scale with the scale expected from the two cameras' resolutions, and rejects the result if it is off by more than a configured factor.
why_it_matters: Catches matches that locked on at the wrong scale (failure mode #13).
done_when: A deliberately wrong-scale match set is rejected with a named reason.

what_it_does: Checks that the source and reference masks are separate objects in memory, not the same one by accident.
why_it_matters: This exact bug faked a competitor's 100% inlier rate (failure mode #19).
done_when: Runs on every execution; deliberately shared masks fail it.

what_it_does: Grades every result from inlier count, inlier ratio, coverage and the control-gate results.
why_it_matters: RANSAC can report 'success' with very few real inliers (failure mode #12).
depends_on: CHECK-01, CHECK-02, CHECK-03, CHECK-04, CHECK-05, CHECK-06, OUT-05, OUT-06, OUT-07
done_when: A deliberately impossible pair returns REJECTED with failure_modes filled in, and the pipeline still exits 0.

what_it_does: The report refuses to render a result with no control-gate results, and a failed run is shown as REJECTED with its reason, never swapped for a quiet fallback.
why_it_matters: Enforces honesty rules H3 and H4: a run without checks is not a valid result.
done_when: A mocked result with empty gates raises an error instead of rendering.

what_it_does: Keeps a register of the 20 known failure modes (PLAN.md section 15), each with a detection hook. Every failure seen at run time is tagged with its mode ID in RegistrationResult.failure_modes. Member B raises the IDs inside the pipeline; Member C owns the register and logger.
why_it_matters: Failures are named and explained instead of hidden.
done_when: Each of the 20 modes has a detection hook or an explicit 'detected manually only' note.

feature: Licence gate (blocks non-commercial models from shipping)
what_it_does: With ship_mode: true (the default), non-commercial models (SuperPoint, SuperGlue) are blocked by name, and R2D2 is never used. SuperGlue runs only in the internal benchmark with ship_mode: false, writing to a folder that is excluded from the shipped bundle. A CI script checks every installed package's licence and the vendored RIFT2 SHA.
why_it_matters: ISRO must be able to legally reuse and redistribute the software (failure mode #14).
done_when: tests/test_licence_gate.py proves superpoint-lightglue is blocked when ship_mode is true and available when false; adding a GPL package fails CI.

what_it_does: Warps the source image into the reference's coordinates and saves it as a GeoTIFF with the correct geotransform and lunar CRS, plus a JSON sidecar holding both images' metadata, the transform and the metrics.
why_it_matters: The 'registered product' the problem statement asks for.
done_when: Opens in QGIS aligned to the reference; warping and then inverse-warping returns within sub-pixel error.

what_it_does: Writes matches.csv: source and reference pixel coordinates (sub-pixel floats, never rounded), lat/lon, confidence, inlier flag, method, regime, cascade stage and grid cell.
why_it_matters: The 'corresponding match points' the problem statement asks for.
done_when: The CSV reads back into a MatchSet without precision loss.

what_it_does: Writes matches.geojson: the match points in the reference frame with the same properties, ready to drop into QGIS.
why_it_matters: Lets the match points be viewed on a map directly.
done_when: Opens in QGIS with the correct lunar CRS.

what_it_does: Average leftover error of the inlier matches after applying the transform, in pixels and in metres (pixels x resolution). Unmeasured = None.
why_it_matters: A metric the problem statement names.
done_when: rmse_px and rmse_m match a hand-calculated fixture.

what_it_does: Number of matches that survive every filtering step.
why_it_matters: A metric the problem statement names.
done_when: inlier_count equals the sum of the inlier mask.

what_it_does: Inliers divided by all candidate matches, between 0 and 1.
why_it_matters: A metric the problem statement names, and the clearest sign of whether a pair is easy or hard.
done_when: inlier_ratio is in [0, 1] and equals inlier_count / total matches.

what_it_does: Fraction of grid cells that contain at least one inlier.
why_it_matters: Shows with a number that the problem statement's even-spread requirement is met.
done_when: spatial_coverage is in [0, 1] and matches a hand-counted fixture.

what_it_does: Measures our own end-to-end time, including tiling and preprocessing, separately from per-matcher time. Published speeds from papers are for planning only and never reported as ours.
why_it_matters: Answers 'how long does it take?' with a measured number.
done_when: runtime_s is measured on every run; end-to-end time is reported separately from matcher time.

what_it_does: One self-contained web page: inputs -> path taken (regime, cascade stages) -> the four problem-statement metrics -> coverage figure -> sub-pixel result -> control-gate table -> confidence tier -> failure modes -> provenance. Missing values show 'not measured', and every number is tagged 'measured' or 'external'.
why_it_matters: The 'evaluation metric' output the problem statement asks for, in a form judges can read.
done_when: make report produces a self-contained HTML file; it refuses to render with empty gates; every number carries a source tag.

what_it_does: Every output records the input product IDs and checksums, config hash, package versions, git commit, UTC time, host/GPU and the ship_mode flag.
why_it_matters: Anyone can trace a number back to the exact inputs and code that produced it.
done_when: Two runs from the same commit and inputs produce identical records apart from the timestamp.

what_it_does: The chandralign command: register, benchmark, ablate, report, demo.
why_it_matters: The 'software' the problem statement asks for.
done_when: --help documents every flag; register runs end to end and writes a run folder.

what_it_does: FastAPI backend: POST /register (runs as a background job), GET /runs/{id}, GET /runs/{id}/assets/{name}, GET /pairs.
why_it_matters: The backend the web interface talks to.
done_when: Returns a valid result for a curated pair within the configured timeout and streams progress.

what_it_does: Pick a curated pair or upload your own, watch the pipeline run, then see the results. Works fully offline from cached runs.
why_it_matters: The demo surface; we assume the venue Wi-Fi will fail.
done_when: The full flow works offline from cached runs.

what_it_does: Source and reference shown next to each other with the sun-angle difference labelled.
why_it_matters: Makes the problem obvious in five seconds; the demo opens on it.
done_when: Renders from both a mock and a real RegistrationResult.

what_it_does: Lines between matched points, with inliers and outliers in different colours (wraps vismatch's plot_matches).
why_it_matters: Shows at a glance which matches the pipeline trusted.
done_when: Renders, and the inlier/outlier counts in the figure match Metrics.

what_it_does: Grid showing how many matches landed in each cell.
why_it_matters: Shows the even-spread requirement being met instead of just claiming it.
done_when: The cell count equals the configured grid, and the occupied fraction equals Metrics.spatial_coverage.

what_it_does: A slider and checkerboard overlay comparing the images before and after alignment.
why_it_matters: Makes the alignment quality visible.
done_when: Renders in both the report and the web interface.

what_it_does: While running: shows which matcher and cascade path were chosen. When done: metric cards (RMSE, inliers, inlier ratio, coverage) and a confidence-tier badge.
why_it_matters: Lets judges watch the pipeline's decisions and results live.
done_when: Metric cards show the same values as the run's Metrics; missing values show 'not measured'.

what_it_does: A REJECTED run shows a clear 'REJECTED - reason' panel with the failure modes that triggered it.
why_it_matters: Hiding failures in the UI would undo honesty rule H3.
done_when: A REJECTED run renders the panel with its reason and failure modes, never an empty results screen.
